clauses.current_legal_basis: The original text of EO 11046 (27 FR 8575) states no end for this clause, and no held later order, statute text or search result revokes or supersedes it (amendments are recorded as later events, not ends). The three selected machine searches (U.S. Code release point 119-121 through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, and the Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record no revocation or supersession of EO 11046. The clause therefore continues on the original text, checked through 2026-10-14.
clauses.reason: Paragraph 1 allows the Bronze Star Medal, first established by EO 9419, to be awarded by the Secretary of a military department or the Secretary of the Treasury for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy, or by designated commanders, to any person serving in or with the armed forces after December 6, 1941 who distinguishes himself by heroic or meritorious achievement or service not involving aerial flight, in the circumstances listed in (a) to (c). Amendments in order: EO 11382 (effective November 28, 1967, 32 FR 16247) replaced the words Secretary of the Treasury with the Secretary of Transportation; EO 13286 section 70 (effective March 1, 2003) replaced the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security; EO 14085 section 4 (effective October 3, 2022, 87 FR 60541) struck Transportation and inserted Homeland Security, struck any person and inserted those individuals, inserted Space Force after Air Force, and struck distinguishes, or has distinguished, himself and inserted the plural form. The clause continues, amended; the changes concern the issuing department and the eligible class, and the award authority continues.

clauses.reason: Paragraph 5 supersedes EO 9419 of February 4, 1944 and keeps existing regulations in effect, so far as not inconsistent, until modified or revoked by regulations prescribed under this order. The supersession of EO 9419 was performed when this order took effect (signed August 24, 1962) and its consequence persists; the continuation sentence ends only when each regulation is modified or revoked, and no held source shows that has happened, so the clause is recorded as operative and no end is assigned.

research_rationale:
EO 11046 (signed August 24, 1962; 27 FR 8575, Federal Register issue of August 28, 1962) authorizes award of the Bronze Star Medal. I read the complete held Federal Register text: five numbered paragraphs (paragraph 1 with sub-items (a) to (c); design and regulations; one medal with devices; posthumous award; supersession of EO 9419 with continuation of existing regulations until modified or revoked). The dossier inventory of eight clauses matches paragraphs 1 to 5 and sub-items (a) to (c), and I confirmed it without correction. Paragraph 1 was amended three times, all held: EO 11382 (signed November 28, 1967; 32 FR 16247) replaced the Secretary of the Treasury with the Secretary of Transportation; EO 13286 section 70 (signed February 28, 2003, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) replaced the Secretary of Transportation with the Secretary of Homeland Security; and EO 14085 section 4 (signed October 3, 2022; 87 FR 60541) struck Transportation for Homeland Security, any person for those individuals, inserted Space Force, and made the verb plural. These are amendments of a continuing clause, not ends, and the sub-items are not touched. The EO 13286 text relied on is the American Presidency Project transcription, disclosed as a working text; the Federal Register copy of EO 13286 that I also read matches it. The U.S. Code prints the order as a note to 10 U.S.C. 7276 with no ending statement (a machine pointer, not relied on as the basis). The three selected searches (U.S. Code through 2026-10-09, eCFR as of 2026-10-14, Federal Register executive-order catalog disposition notes) record only the three amendments and no revocation or supersession. All clauses are operative as amended, checked through 2026-10-14.
